responsibility: rustc_ast_passes provides the compiler’s AST-level checking and inspection passes that run after parsing and macro expansion but before HIR lowering. Its lib.rs root defines the crate surface, wiring together the validation, feature-gating, node-counting, and span-debugging functionality, keeping diagnostics support internal, and loading the Fluent messages those passes use. ast_validation.rs implements the core post-expansion AST validation pass, walking the finalized AST to ensure items, types, traits, impls, extern blocks, generics, patterns, and related forms are structurally and syntactically valid and reporting whether proc-macro declarations are present. feature_gate.rs enforces language and attribute stability at the AST level by traversing crate syntax and attributes, diagnosing unstable or incompatible features, ABI forms, and syntax extensions, and enforcing channel restrictions such as disallowing `#![feature]` on non-nightly compilers. errors.rs centralizes the structured diagnostics, notes, suggestions, and supporting enums/subdiagnostics used by these passes and by span-debugging output. node_count.rs supplies a lightweight AST visitor for roughly measuring crate size by counting visited nodes, supporting diagnostic or debugging-oriented compiler uses. show_span.rs provides a developer debugging visitor that walks selected AST node kinds and emits diagnostics showing their source spans. Together, these components make rustc_ast_passes the crate responsible for validating, feature-checking, and introspecting the Rust AST so later compiler stages receive a well-formed, policy-compliant input.
